- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33) or shows sharp decline, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk reversal.  
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (especially >75% of recent high); apply a “cool-down” factor: cap forecast at 10% below recent peak.  
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.33–0.75), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast toward historical 30-day average if deviation >2σ.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven corrections; apply a “sentiment-weighted lag” correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for each day of negative sentiment trend.  
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.25) over 5+ days, model underperforms; increase forecast by 2–4% to account for suppressed volatility.
